title: La Vang (Vietnam)
hookLine: Catholics hiding from persecution in 1798 remember Mary appearing in the forest

lines: A POT OF LEAVES OVER A FIRE.
cards: A pot of leaves is boiling over a small fire, deep in a forest in the hills of central Vietnam. Around it sit families who have left their villages.
They are Catholics, and in their country, at this time, being Catholic could cost you your home or your life. So they've come to the trees to hide. Some are sick with fever.
There's no doctor, no medicine, and nowhere safer to go. At night they pray the rosary together, quietly. The leaves in that pot have a story, and Vietnamese Catholics still tell it.

teach.h: A CHURCH HIDING IN THE TREES.
teach.b: First, the hiding. Tradition says that during a time of persecution, Catholics fled into the forest at La Vang.

The Letter to the Hebrews describes believers like them, in the Douay-Rheims: "wandering in deserts, in mountains, and in dens, and in caves of the earth." A church without a building, praying under the trees.

teach.h: A MOTHER WITH A CHILD, AND AN ANSWER.
teach.b: Tradition says that as they prayed, a lady appeared among the branches, holding a child, with angels beside her. She didn't promise them their villages back, or that their persecutors would fall.

She comforted them and told them what to do: gather the leaves from the trees around them and boil them as medicine for the sick. Third, the leaves. That small, practical instruction echoes the Bible's last chapter.
In John's vision of the heavenly city, the tree of life grows by the river, and "the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations."

At La Vang, by the people's memory, the healing came from the ordinary trees they were hiding under. In the story, heaven doesn't lift them out of the forest; it meets them in it. Fourth, the keeping.

Tradition says the survivors remembered, and built a small chapel on the spot, and pilgrims still gather under the trees as those families did. Like every apparition, La Vang asks no one to believe it.

teach.h: THE LEAVES OF THE TREE WERE FOR THE HEALING OF THE NATIONS.
teach.b: What it hands on is a picture: a mother finding her children exactly where they were hiding.

how: Catholics in Vietnam and abroad honor Our Lady of La Vang; pilgrims travel to the shrine at La Vang in central Vietnam to pray, and Vietnamese Catholic communities elsewhere keep images of her in their churches.

games.q: you're hiding in the forest with your family. people are sick with fever and there's no doctor. the lady appears. what does she tell you?
o: leave the forest and go home.
boil the leaves of these trees as medicine.
games.why: tradition says she told them to boil the leaves from the trees around them. the help was already within reach, in the forest where they hid.

practice: Bring Vietnam to mind, its cities, villages, forests and coast, and its Catholics past and present, including those who once prayed in hiding; then widen it to anyone, anywhere, who has to hide what they believe today.
Hold them gently, the way the families held the sick by that fire. If you pray, pray a decade of the rosary for Vietnam; if not, hold its people in mind, one breath at a time.

wordCard.voice: La Vang. The forest in Vietnam where, tradition says, Mary came to Catholics hiding from persecution and told them to boil the leaves as medicine. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: in the forest. The medicine was in the leaves overhead. See you tomorrow.
